To calculate the cost difference between the two processes we start with a base- case cost analysis model for producing a 24.8% TOPCon cell from a ~260 mm diameter boule (M10 wafer) at a scale of 2.5 GW/year in the US. Using the standard model for a Siemens + Cz-produced n-type wafer in the Detailed Cost Analysis Model (DCAM) [12] program (specifically: 2025 Benchmark Ingot and Wafer Cost Model), we calculate the factory-level and total $/W costs for the cells (Table II). For Page 20 of 30 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. the Fz-CVD analysis we assumed the same 24.8% efficient TOPCon cell process but changed the wafer production process to account for the Fz-CVD inputs by either calculating or estimating a new values based on our CFD modeling, literature values, or input from industry experts. We assumed a poly-Si growth rate of 120 µm/min to match our modeled growth results. Table II, second column, shows the output of the DCAM for the base-case Fz-CVD process. To complete the technoeconomic model to show energy production benefits, we used the online Comparative PV Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) calculator [13]. This program allows for a simple comparison between two products to calculate an LCOE difference. All inputs were held constant in the calculator between the two compared modules except cell cost ($/m2 – input from DCAM), module efficiency, system degradation rate, and service life – see Table III for inputs.
